newsitem.title: UK: Next chief rejects Sears job-paper.
newsitem.headline: Next chief rejects Sears job-paper.

text.p: The boss of fashion retailing chain Next Plc was offered the job of chief executive at Sears Plc, the struggling UK retailer, but has rejected the approach said a report in the Sunday Telegraph.
The unsourced report claimed David Jones, Next chief executive, was approached in recent days along with bosses at two other blue chip firms who also rebuffed the offer.

Sears' current chief executive Liam Strong has seen his position come under attack for failing to revive the fortunes of the sprawling retail empire which spans shoes to the flagship department store Selfridges in London.

Analysts last week said that a number of institutional investors were baying for Strong's blood despite efforts by the group to return some shareholder value through the sale of the Freemans mail order firm and a promise of a 410 million stg cash handout.

City of London headhunters have been putting out feelers for a possible successor, said the report, but no one was claiming responsibility for their actions amid some suggestions that major investors are planning to mount a coup.
In recent weeks Sears issued a profit warning, saying profits would fall below last year's 100 million stg level, said the report.
